title: Applied ML Evals: Unified Standards and Playbooks
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates standards, checklists, and playbooks for Applied ML evaluation at Redwood Inference. It covers the eval harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profiles, and the regression triage process. The goal is a single reference engineering teams can use to onboard models, maintain evaluation hygiene, and resolve regressions quickly with clear ownership and measurable SLOs.

Audience
- ML Engineers, Applied ML, Platform Engineers, Reliability Engineers, and Product Owners working on model serving and evaluation.

Principles
- Reproducibility: every evaluation must be reproducible from source prompt set and harness version.
- Measurability: define concrete, actionable metrics (EM, F1, ROUGE, perplexity, latency, cost-per-token).
- Safety-first: include guardrails for safety, privacy and PII handling in every onboarding.
- Cost-awareness: recommend quantization/batching tradeoffs only when verified by benchmarks.

Components and Responsibilities
1) Eval Harness
- Owner: Applied ML (primary) + Eng DevEx (support for infra).
- Purpose: provide reproducible test execution, dataset versioning, metric calculation, and regression detection.
- Artifacts: harness repo tag, CI job (eval-runner), canonical metrics schema (see below), stored artifacts in s3://redwood-evals/{model}/{run_id}/.
- Key Requirements:
  - CI must run full onboarding eval (see Onboarding checklist) and smoke tests on every model-serving release.
  - Harness must support seed-controlled randomness and record environment (CUDA/cuDNN, GPU type, python, library versions).
  - Outputs: metrics.json (schema v2), artifacts.tar.gz, and a deterministic HTML summary.

Metrics schema (summary)\- All harness outputs must include:
  - run_id: stable string
  - model: model identifier (catalog id + config)
  - version: model artifact version or git tag
  - prompt_set_id: canonical prompt set name
  - metrics: list of metric entries with name, value, unit, and confidence_interval where applicable
  - latencies: p50/p95/p99 per-sequence and per-token
  - resource_profile: gpu_type, batch_size, memory_peak_mb

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmarks
- Owner: Applied ML + Product for domain-specific sets.
- Purpose: maintain curated prompt sets for onboarding, regression detection, and targeted benchmarks (NLP, summarization, retrieval-augmented QA, instruction-following, code generation).
- Organization: prompt sets live in the prompt-sets monorepo with metadata: intent, acceptance-criteria, source, dataset-license, and canonical seed(s).

Prompt set acceptance criteria (high level)
- Representative: covers common production input distributions (min 500 examples for narrow domain, 2k+ for general-purpose).
- Annotated: each example has expected outputs (gold or heuristics), and tags for edge cases and safety.
- Versioned: new additions require changelog and review.

Benchmarks and SLOs\- Baseline acceptance SLOs for onboarding (example):
  - Task accuracy/EM: >= baseline_model_score + delta (delta depends on product; default delta = -2% for parity).
  - Latency: p95 <= 2x baseline latency for same HW and batch config.
  - Cost: estimated tokens-per-second and cost-per-1000-tokens must be documented.
  - Safety: zero tolerable rate for high-severity safety violations on curated safety test sets.

3) Model Onboarding Guide (Quick checklist)
- Owner: Applied ML (lead) + Eng Platform (infra).
- Checklist (must pass before model is accepted onto hosted catalog or Dedicated):
  1. Model artifact stored in model registry with digest, provenance, and license.
 2. Run full eval-harness onboarding suite (functional, domain, safety, latency, stress) and upload artifacts.
 3. Provide quantization profiles and recommended runtime configs.
 4. Document known failure modes and mitigation strategies.
 5. Security review: confirm no embedded secrets, ensure license compliance.
 6. Product sign-off: Product reviewer confirms metric tradeoffs acceptable.
 7. Release note template filled: model name, version, changes, expected performance delta, and rollback plan.

Onboarding CI job example (CLI)
- run: eval-runner --model-id redwood/open-model-v1 --prompt-set onboarding-general-v1 --out s3://redwood-evals/open-model-v1/onboard-2026-04-15/ --profile full

4) Quality Guardrails
- Owner: Applied ML + Security for privacy guardrails.
- Guardrail types:
  - Content safety: toxic generation tests, PII leakage detection, hallucination heuristics.
  - Data handling: ensure prompt and eval outputs are handled per data-retention policy (refer to /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention).
  - Output constraints: tools/calling interfaces must validate structured output schemas.

Examples (safety rules)
- High-severity toxic output: immediate fail.
- PII exposure: any detected sequence with high-confidence PII match must be flagged and reviewed.

5) Quantization Profiles
- Owner: Research/Applied ML (lead) + Eng Serving Runtime (ops).
- Purpose: standardized profiles to balance quality and cost for supported hardware.
- Each profile must be documented with: profile_name, numeric precision, supported hardware, expected quality delta (vs fp16 baseline), memory reduction, recommended batch sizes, and sample cbind commands.

Representative quantization table (human-readable)
| profile_name | precision | supported_hardware | expected_quality_delta | memory_reduction | recommended_use_case | notes |
|-------------|-----------|--------------------|------------------------|------------------|----------------------|-------|
| q8_0        | 8-bit     | A100, H100         | -1.5% (instr)         | ~3x               | LLM instruction-serving | fast inference with slight quality drop |
| q4_0        | 4-bit     | A100, H100, T4     | -3.0%                 | ~6x               | high-throughput embeddings | use with cache-heavy workloads |
| fp16        | 16-bit    | all GPUs           | 0.0%                  | 1.8x             | default for latency-sensitive workloads | baseline |

Quantization verification steps (required)
1. Run quantized evals for the same prompt sets as onboarding and produce metrics.json.
2. Compare quality deltas: if > allowed_delta for target use-case, profile is not recommended.
3. Include memory/latency measurements and a checklist for HW-specific kernel fallbacks.

6) Regression Triage Playbook
- Owner: Eng SRE + Applied ML.
- Purpose: standardized triage and rollback flow for model performance regressions discovered via CI, monitoring, or customer reports.

Alerting thresholds (examples)
- functional-metric-regression: relative drop >= 5% over baseline window (7 days) -> page SRE_oncall and AppliedML_oncall.
- latency-regression: p95 increased by >= 50% over baseline -> page SRE_oncall.
- safety-violation: any high-severity violation -> immediate page to PagerDuty + product security.

Triage flow (numbered)
1. Acknowledge alert and record run_id and metric snapshot.
2. Reproduce: trigger eval-runner with the same harness version and prompt set.
3. Isolate cause: compare metrics across model version, quantization profile, batch config, and runtime kernel. Use diff-metrics tool: diff-metrics --baseline s3://redwood-evals/{model}/baseline/metrics.json --target s3://redwood-evals/{model}/{run_id}/metrics.json
4. If root cause is model change (new weights): notify product, create rollback plan, and if needed, run canary rollback (A/B) with 10% traffic and 24h observation.
5. If root cause is infra/kernel/quantization: escalate to Eng Serving Runtime and schedule hotfix or kernel fallback.
6. Document postmortem within 72 hours if regression affected production traffic or customer SLAs.

Postmortem template (requirements)
- Summary (1-2 sentences)
- Impact (users, endpoints, duration)
- Timeline of events (UTC timestamps)
- Root cause analysis and evidence (artifacts)
- Corrective actions and owner with ETA
- Preventative actions (SLOs, tests added to harness)

Operational integrations and CI
- CI gating: model onboarding job must pass a subset of smoke metrics (latency p95 and basic accuracy) before merge to prod-catalog.
- Monitoring: export metrics to prometheus/grafana; key dashboards: model-performance (accuracy trends), model-latency (p50/p95/p99), model-safety (violations/time).
- Canary config: default canary ramp = 5% for 6 hours -> 25% for 18 hours -> 100% if stable. Configured via redwood-deploy/canary.yaml.

References and artifacts
- Canonical prompt-sets repo: git@github.com:redwood-evals/prompt-sets.git
- Eval harness: git@github.com:redwood-evals/eval-harness.git (see README for metrics schema)
- Quantization profiles: s3://redwood-artifacts/quant-profiles/v1/
- Regression alerting playbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process

Operational contact list
- Applied ML on-call: #applied-ml-oncall (Slack) and PagerDuty: applied-ml-pd
- Eng SRE on-call: #eng-sre-oncall and PagerDuty: eng-sre-pd
- Security: security-oncall@redwood.com

Appendix: Example commands and snippets
- Run a focused regression reproduction:
  eval-runner --model-id redwood/open-model-v2 --prompt-set regression-core-2026 --out ./out/regress-run/ --profile q8_0 --seed 42
- Fetch and compare metrics:
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-evals/open-model-v2/baseline/metrics.json ./baseline.json
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-evals/open-model-v2/onboard-2026-04-15/metrics.json ./target.json
  diff-metrics --base baseline.json --target target.json --out ./diff-report.json

Contributing and governance
- Changes to any canon artifacts (prompt sets, quant profiles, harness metrics schema) require a design doc, review by at least two Applied ML reviewers, and a scheduled sync in the weekly Eval Standards meeting.
- Major changes (schema/metrics semantics/thresholds) must be approved by the Applied ML manager and Eng Platform lead.

This playbook is the single source of truth for evaluation hygiene across Redwood Inference. Updates should be made via PR to the prompt-sets or eval-harness repos and referenced here.
